identificationModule.briefTitle: Safety and Efficacy Study of Dronabinol to Treat Obstructive Sleep Apnea
identificationModule.officialTitle: Cannabimimetic Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Proof of Concept Trial

collaborators.name: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI)

descriptionModule.briefSummary: This is a proof of concept study to determine the safety and efficacy of dronabinol for the treatment of obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (OSA).

armGroups.label: Sugar Pill
armGroups.description: Placebo, once per day (QD) by mouth, 60 minutes before bedtime for 6 weeks after 1-week run-in

armGroups.label: 2.5 mg/day
armGroups.description: Dronabinol, 2.5 mg QD by mouth, 60 minutes before bedtime for 6 weeks after 1-week placebo run-in

armGroups.label: 10 mg/day
armGroups.description: Dronabinol, 10 mg QD by mouth, 60 minutes before bedtime for 4 weeks after 1-week placebo run-in and 2-week dose escalation

primaryOutcomes.description: Change in AHI derived as: AHI (end of treatment) minus AHI (pre-treatment)

Change in ESS derived as: ESS (end of treatment) minus ESS (pre-treatment). The ESS scale has a range of 0 to 24, with 0 representing the least degree of sleepiness and 24 the greatest degree of sleepiness. There are no subscales.

primaryOutcomes.measure: Change in Sleep Latency: Maintenance of Wakefulness Test (MWT)
primaryOutcomes.description: Change in MWT derived as: MWT (end of treatment) minus MWT (pre-treatment). The Maintenance of Wakefulness Test measures a person's ability to stay awake in a quiet, dark and nonstimulating room for a period of time.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Tolerability by Treatment Satisfaction Questionnaire for Medications (TSQM) Overall Score.
secondaryOutcomes.description: The TSQM measures a person's satisfaction with treatment based on a 7-point scale ranging from "Extremely Dissatisfied" to "Extremely Satisfied" in response to the question, "Taking all things into account, how satisfied or dissatisfied are you with this medication?".
AEs will be evaluated and tracked throughout subject participation (up to 8 weeks)
Change in DT (total minutes with arterial oxygen saturation below 85% during 8-hour polysomnography) derived as: DT (end of treatment) minus DT (pre-treatment)
